reason: A offers the more physically credible controlled intervention: mild annealing can reduce residual strain and defect density while preserving phase, whereas low-energy ion irradiation generally creates defects rather than reliably healing or homogenizing them. Both proposals have a mechanistic inconsistency—narrowing the distribution of local exchange/transition conditions would normally sharpen, not broaden, the transition—and A is somewhat incremental relative to prior annealing work, but it remains the more feasible and decisive study.
